I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou County best. On my farm, that is still the most reliable way to use the full year, spread labor, and protect income. I will carry winter wheat through to harvest, then plant summer maize right after. I am 66, so I do not want a complicated crop mix that adds management risk. I have enough education to follow improved practices closely, so I will use better seed, moderate but sufficient fertilizer, irrigation only when it matters, and pest control based on field conditions rather than spraying blindly. For tillage, I will keep it practical: rotary tillage for wheat establishment and mostly no-tillage for summer maize after wheat so I can save time and hold soil moisture. My goal is stable yield, manageable workload, and efficient input use rather than chasing the highest possible output.
